Question: Does the multilingual demand for this feature extend beyond the UI chrome to answer & source language (insights 101, 214, 43), and if so, should scope widen?
Recommended Approach: e.g. Survey
Risk without / Expected Impact with Rese: Refresh 2026-08-19: the answer-language insights now carry 33 votes against the selector's 6, and the database holds 15 language insights / 60 mentions in total. Risk without: the selector ships and the actual complaint is untouched. Impact with: scope is set against where the demand really sits.

Question: When a user sets a UI language, what do they expect to happen to answers, citations and uploaded documents — does the setting govern all of them?
Recommended Approach: Concept test of the selector with three interpretations of scope
Risk without / Expected Impact with Rese: Risk without: the selector is read as a global language switch and generates support load when answers stay mixed (insight 214). Impact with: the setting's promise matches its behaviour.

Question: For Swiss and cross-border users, must retrieval stay language-agnostic regardless of the UI setting (insights 414, 221, 465)?
Recommended Approach: Interviews with the Swiss Publisher account plus 2–3 cross-border Corporate/Big Law users, using real multilingual mandates
Risk without / Expected Impact with Rese: Risk without: a language setting silently narrows the source corpus and turns a preference into incomplete legal research. Impact with: the boundary between interface language and retrieval language is defined before it is coded.

Question: Is the real ask behind “appropriate language” (insight 101, 18 mentions) a language setting at all, or German legal register — Rubrum, Anschreiben, Gutachtenstil, citation style (insight 459)?
Recommended Approach: Document analysis of user-corrected outputs + interviews with the Lime Survey respondents who reported register errors
Risk without / Expected Impact with Rese: Risk without: the largest language cluster in the database is filed under a setting that cannot address it. Impact with: register and citation convention are scoped as their own workstream.

Question: Which concrete tasks are blocked (not just slowed) for screen-reader and keyboard-only users across chat, Matrix Analysis and the Word add-in?
Recommended Approach: Moderated usability test with assistive-technology users
Risk without / Expected Impact with Rese: Risk without: the SVA gap analysis is remediated at component level while whole legal workflows stay unusable end-to-end. Impact with: a ranked, workflow-level remediation backlog instead of a WCAG checklist.

Question: Do our public-sector and judiciary customers carry a procurement-level accessibility requirement (BITV 2.0 / EN 301 549) that Noxtua must evidence?
Recommended Approach: Structured interviews with procurement / IT contacts at existing public-sector accounts
Risk without / Expected Impact with Rese: Risk without: an accessibility conformance statement is requested in a tender and cannot be substantiated. Impact with: requirements are known before they become deal-blockers.

Question: Why has accessibility produced zero of 383 insights and zero of 293 Featurebase posts — is demand genuinely absent, or are affected users absent from our feedback channels?
Recommended Approach: Audit of feedback-channel reach + screener question in the next survey wave
Risk without / Expected Impact with Rese: Risk without: a silent-population blind spot is mistaken for low demand and the item is deprioritised on false evidence. Impact with: we learn whether the absence of signal is real.

Question: What is the minimum accessible baseline for AI-specific interaction patterns (streaming answers, live-updating Matrix cells, inline citations) that no WCAG success criterion describes well?
Recommended Approach: Expert review with the external agency + literature scan
Risk without / Expected Impact with Rese: Risk without: standard remediation passes the audit but the AI-specific surfaces remain unusable. Impact with: reusable interaction patterns for every future AI feature.

Question: Do the features marked implemented (tracked changes 255, supporting documents 392, add-in chat history 393/394) actually work in the field — post 487 still reports failures from 2026-07-23?
Recommended Approach: Verification test of the released behaviour with 5 add-in users, against the original insight wording
Risk without / Expected Impact with Rese: Risk without: stabilisation is scoped around features believed to be done, and the same complaints keep arriving through support. Impact with: the difference between “released” and “works” is measured before the sprint is planned.

Question: Which web-app capabilities do add-in users actually miss in the drafting moment, and in what order — is the named set (@mentioning, EU License, Voice Input) the right one?
Recommended Approach: Parity audit + contextual inquiry with 5 heavy add-in users
Risk without / Expected Impact with Rese: Risk without: parity is delivered as a feature checklist while the real friction sits elsewhere. Impact with: the stabilisation scope is ordered by workflow cost, not by list order.

Question: How often does the session actually drop, and does the auto-logout (insight 472) correlate with abandonment of the add-in for that document?
Recommended Approach: Telemetry analysis on session length and re-authentication events
Risk without / Expected Impact with Rese: Risk without: a 6-vote report is treated as an irritation when it may be the single largest driver of add-in churn. Impact with: the defect is sized and can be prioritised against feature parity honestly.

Question: Is voice input in the add-in a genuinely distinct need from voice input in the web app (short prompting vs. long dictation — insight 519 vs. the 15-vote Voice Input for Prompting card)?
Recommended Approach: Comparative concept test with dictation-heavy vs. typing-heavy users
Risk without / Expected Impact with Rese: Risk without: one voice implementation is built for a 30-second prompt and fails the dictation use case entirely. Impact with: scope is split correctly before engineering starts.

Question: Insight 378 (folders) is marked implemented, yet the “Template Organisation” card still asks for collections, grouping and tags — what does the shipped feature not cover?
Recommended Approach: Walkthrough of the released organisation feature with users who raised 378, against the card's wording
Risk without / Expected Impact with Rese: Risk without: the rework rebuilds something already shipped, or ships a second organisation model beside the first. Impact with: the card is either scoped precisely or closed as done.

Question: Is the low template adoption caused by creation friction (the 498–504/527 cluster) or by a mismatch between templates and how the work is actually structured?
Recommended Approach: Funnel analysis on template creation + follow-up interviews with users who abandoned creation
Risk without / Expected Impact with Rese: Risk without: the UI is reworked, friction drops, and adoption still does not move because the concept — not the form — is the barrier. Impact with: the rework targets the actual drop-off.

Question: For private templates, what is the expected sharing lifecycle — does a private template ever get promoted to a team or company template, and who approves that?
Recommended Approach: Concept test of two governance models (personal-only vs. promotable) with Corporate vs. Law Firm users
Risk without / Expected Impact with Rese: Risk without: private templates ship as a dead end and firms rebuild governance outside the tool. Impact with: the permission model is designed once rather than retrofitted (insights 301, 379).

Question: Should user input be optional by default, and what does a template do when the input is skipped — prompt, guess, or fail?
Recommended Approach: Prototype test of the apply-template flow with and without required inputs
Risk without / Expected Impact with Rese: Risk without: making input optional (the Product Board card) trades one confusion for another at apply time (insight 504). Impact with: one coherent behaviour across creation and application.

Question: Which DMS actually holds the authoritative file per segment — iManage/NetDocuments (Big Law), SharePoint (Corporate), DATEV (Small Law) — and what is the volume behind each?
Recommended Approach: Account-level survey of existing customers + pipeline review with Sales
Risk without / Expected Impact with Rese: Risk without: the “first integration” is chosen on technical convenience and serves the smaller half of the 19-vote demand. Impact with: the sequencing decision is evidence-based and defensible to customers.

Question: Must the integration be bidirectional (read + file back), or is read-only enough for a first release?
Recommended Approach: Workflow mapping interviews with knowledge managers, following one mandate end to end
Risk without / Expected Impact with Rese: Risk without: a read-only v1 ships and the copy-back step keeps users in the old workflow, suppressing measured adoption. Impact with: the MVP boundary is drawn where the workflow actually closes.

Question: How must DMS permissions and ethical walls be mirrored, and what will customers' security teams require before approving a connector?
Recommended Approach: Structured interviews with IT security / DPO at 3–4 accounts, plus review of two real security questionnaires
Risk without / Expected Impact with Rese: Risk without: a functionally complete integration is blocked in security review, or worse, surfaces documents across an ethical wall (insight 345). Impact with: requirements enter the concept phase instead of the escalation phase.

Question: Is the underlying need document access, or knowledge-base grounding on the firm's own corpus (insights 340, 74 — 26 votes) — and are those the same project?
Recommended Approach: Jobs-to-be-done interviews distinguishing “fetch this file” from “know our precedents”
Risk without / Expected Impact with Rese: Risk without: a file-picker is built when users expected retrieval over the whole corpus, and the 26-vote custom-data demand stays unmet. Impact with: two adjacent roadmap items are scoped apart deliberately.
